episodes.158913: A moderately unstable air mass and high moisture lead to scattered showers and thunderstorms across the region. A few storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.159000: Thunderstorms developed and trained along a stalled front in a high moisture environment leading to a report of flash flooding.
episodes.159101: Severe winds were measured from outflow thunderstorm winds from a storm in Eureka County.
episodes.159105: Slow moving and training thunderstorms moved across central Mississippi during the morning hours of July 19th. Heavy rainfall resulted in flash flooding across portions of east central Mississippi.
episodes.159194: A band of showers and thunderstorms developed during the early morning hours of July 19th across portions of Southeast Oklahoma and Southwest Arkansas, near a weak surface front and associated upper level trough that slowly sank south into East Texas and North Louisiana by/shortly after daybreak. Given the high moisture content available, adequate forcing aloft and available weak to moderate instability contributed to these storms becoming efficient rainfall producers, resulting in periods of heavy rain falling over portions of East Texas as additional showers and thunderstorms developed and spread southeast over the same areas of East Texas even through the early afternoon. Widespread rainfall amounts of three to six inches fell across Smith and Gregg Counties, with isolated higher amounts in excess of seven inches recorded over Northern Smith County. This resulted in flash flooding across the cities of Lindale and Longview, with high water rescues needed for stranded motorists in the flood waters. These showers and thunderstorms eventually diminished during the mid and late afternoon hours with the passage of the weak front.
episodes.159245: Thunderstorms trained across the city of Decatur, AL for several hours on the evening of the 18th into the 19th. Decatur is notorious for flash flooding, with scattered reports occurring in the wake of 3-5 of rainfall in a couple of hours.
episodes.159330: A thunderstorm moved north along the coast and produced strong winds along the barrier island, affecting Ormond-by-the-Sea.
episodes.159695: A disorganized north-south oriented line of showers and storms developed along the Route 15 corridor during the afternoon of July 19, 2021. One of the storms in this broken line produced a report of wind damage in Perry County.
episodes.159706: Deep west to southwest flow prevailed throughout the column and widespread|showers and storms quickly moved inland from the Gulf coast in the late|morning to early afternoon hours toward the east coast. A weak east coast sea breeze was near the Atlantic coast, and convergence of the sea breezes and outflow boundaries resulted in storm to storm storms with enhancement from a passing shortwave aloft.
episodes.159707: Deep west to southwest flow prevailed throughout the column and widespread|showers and storms quickly moved inland from the Gulf coast in the late|morning to early afternoon hours toward the east coast. A weak east coast sea breeze was near the Atlantic coast, and convergence of the sea breezes and outflow boundaries resulted in storm to storm storms with enhancement from a passing shortwave aloft.
episodes.159742: On the morning of July 19, 2021, between 10 and 10:30am CDT, a line of sub-severe thunderstorms caused a canoe with two occupants to capsize. Neither were wearing life jackets and one of the two occupants drowned. The incident occurred on Loon Lake east of Crane Lake, Minnesota, within the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness (BWCAW). Estimated wind speeds along the line of storms were 25-30 mph based on nearby observations.
episodes.159809: Numerous thunderstorms developed in the late afternoon hours across inland areas and moved toward the coast in the evening. These thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the coast and over the Atlantic coastal waters.
episodes.160166: Thunderstorms produced isolated flash flooding. The storms occurred in the vicinity of a 500 mb trough that extended from the eastern Great Lakes southwest across the lower Ohio Valley. The convection itself was induced by a remnant mesoscale vorticity center that moved eastward from Missouri. The storms formed in an increasingly moist and unstable air mass. The wind flow aloft was weak, causing the storm motion to be driven by mesoscale processes. The storms propagated slowly east to southeast.
episodes.160323: During the afternoon of July 18th, monsoonal related storms moved into the combined Oklahoma and Texas Panhandles as an upper-level disturbance moved south into the Oklahoma Panhandle during the early afternoon hours. Though widespread severe weather did not occur on this day, a couple of isolated storms produced destructive winds. The storms continued to move south over the eastern Texas Panhandle gradually weakening however one final severe wind gust did occur near Wellington, TX.
episodes.160847: High pressure was situated just northeast of the area with diurnally forced cumulus. Increased thermal advection created enough instability for a couple brief funnel clouds to develop in the vicinity of the Des Moines metro.
episodes.160889: A slow-moving thunderstorm produced torrential rainfall across the Village of Fonda on Monday, July 19, 2021. Between 3 and 4 inches of rain fell in just a couple of hours. A small creek north of the village overflowed its banks, sending water and mud downstream into the village. Storm drains became plugged up with debris so water was unable to get through. Many roads were closed and impassable in and around the village until early Tuesday morning, July 20, 2021. ||A state of emergency was issued in the Village of Fonda as a result of the flooding.||In addition, this thunderstorm produced 1 inch hail near Johnstown, NY.
episodes.160980: A late season cold front moved into South Central Texas and generated thunderstorms. One of these storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.161063: Showers and thunderstorms formed along a weak cold front as it pushed south through the area on Monday, July 19. One storms produced minor wind damage in Bell County.
episodes.161097: A similar pattern to the previous day saw thunderstorms develop along a southward moving outflow boundary during the afternoon of the 18th, with one report of severe wind and hail received.
episodes.161146: A relatively stationary front meandered across southern New England on the 17th and 18th while low pressure slowly moved along the front.  At upper levels, an upper low was moving slowly eastward from the Great Lakes.  With very moisture-laden air in place across the region, the result was heavy rain and flash flooding. In addition, there were rounds of severe thunderstorms and even a weak tornado in northern Connecticut. Rainfall totals ranged from 3.0 to 5.6 inches in northern Connecticut and western and central Massachusetts.  Mainly 1.0 to 2.0 inches fell in Rhode Island and eastern Massachusetts.
episodes.161168: A persistent ridge across the Desert Southwest allowed for enhanced monsoonal moisture across Southern California from July 17-19. A Flash Flood Watch was issued for the Riverside County Mountains and the San Diego County Mountains for July 18. Thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall in the mountains, where several flood advisories were issued on July 17 and July 18. A cluster of elevated thunderstorms formed across northern San Diego County and progressed westward to the coast early on the morning of July 18.
episodes.161211: Showers and thunderstorms formed in a tropical air-mass along a stalled cold front to create flooding and flash flooding.
episodes.161245: An active monsoon surge brought several back-to-back days of thunderstorms producing heavy rain, damaging wind gusts, and hail across the state.
episodes.161262: A warm and humid airmass remained stagnant over Central New York on this day. A weak upper level disturbance moved through the region, triggering heavy rain producing thunderstorms. Steering winds were very weak, therefore, thunderstorms lingered over the same areas resulting in urban and small stream flash flooding.
episodes.161303: Thunderstorms developed during the evening hours over north central North Dakota along a variety of surface boundaries moving through the area. This was in an environment of very strong instability and deep layer shear. A few storms became severe, with the most intense storms occurring over McHenry County where reports of baseball size hail and estimated wind gusts to 75 mph occurred.
episodes.161366: In the afternoon hours on July 19th, an outflow boundary raced south interacting with a moist, unstable airmass settled across the region. This led to widespread showers and strong thunderstorms to develop, with an isolated severe thunderstorm over Washington Parish.
episodes.161391: A big push of monsoon moisture led to ten days of scattered thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert. Many storms produced flash flooding and/or high winds. Events in this episode are continued in the July 22-26 Thunderstorms episode.
episodes.161392: A big push of monsoon moisture led to five days of scattered thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert and the Sierra. Many storms produced flash flooding and/or high winds.
episodes.161393: A big push of monsoon moisture led to ten days of scattered thunderstorms over the Mojave Desert and southern Great Basin. Many storms produced flash flooding and/or high winds. Events in this episode are continued in the July 22-26 Thunderstorms episode.
episodes.161439: An elongated upper trough extended from east Texas northeast across northwest Alabama and eastern Tennessee.  Precipitable water values exceeded two inches along and south of the upper trough axis.  Several clusters of convection with locally heavy rainfall produced flash flooding in Jefferson and Shelby counties.
episodes.161609: Slow moving thunderstorms developed across Cochise, Graham and Greenlee counties during the afternoon. Heavy rain up to 2 inches per hour caused areas of flash flooding.
episodes.161679: A few thunderstorms produced isolated damaging wind in Jones County.
episodes.161842: A wave of low pressure tracked along a stalled front across portions of the southern Coastal Plain. The combination of day time heating and the aforementioned frontal forcing and moisture pooling along the front lead to the development of heavy rain and isolated flash flooding in Sampson County.
episodes.162096: Organized convection developed across northern Arizona with heavy rain and rotation in some storms.
